_comment: Reviewed pairings from this page's foods to Frida 6.1 rows, by FoodID.
77 of the 78 proposals in FRIDA-MAP-REVIEW.md, banked on 2026-08-21 after
every one was read against the corpus a second time, this time with the
release's Danish name and EFSA classification in hand. FRIDA-BANKING-REVIEW.md
records what each decision was and why. Asparagus is the one refusal.
Fields. `name` and `name_danish` are the row's own, carried so that a FoodID
pointing somewhere else after a release is visible rather than silent. The
Danish one is not decoration: 24, 559 and 606 are all named "Carrot, raw" in
English, so `name` alone cannot say which was banked. `match` is exact, close
or proxy, and a proxy is marked on the page. `reviewed` must be true: the pass
that reads this file refuses an entry without it, the way tools/flavonoids.mjs
refuses an unreviewed usda-map.json entry. `note` is present where the pairing
took a decision rather than a nod.
Candidates are in FRIDA-MAP-REVIEW.md and proposed-page-map-frida.json,
written by `node tools/frida.mjs propose`. A tool may propose a pairing and
only a human may bank one.

chickpeas-cooked.name: Chickpeas, steamed, ready to eat
chickpeas-cooked.note: Frida has no chickpea boiled from dry: 1812 is canned and 1813 is steamed ready to eat. Banked as a proxy because the kidney bean rows show what that difference costs, 205 against 13 on molybdenum between the ready-to-eat and dried-and-boiled forms of one bean in one report.

kidney-beans-cooked.name: Beans, red kidney, dried and boiled
kidney-beans-cooked.name_danish: Bønner, røde kidney, tørret og kogt
kidney-beans-cooked.note: 1811 "cooked, ready to eat" led on file order. Both rows classify as a boiled dry kidney bean, and 1816 "tørret og kogt" is the one prepared the way this page's is, matching CoFID 13-659 and AFCD F000451 and the parallel white-bean row 1815. Their molybdenum differs 16x, 13 against 205, which is the reason a ready-to-eat product is not a substitute.

tofu-firm.name: Tofu, soy bean curd
tofu-firm.note: Frida's only tofu, unqualified on firmness, which is water content against a figure per 100 g.

peanuts.name: Peanut, dried
peanuts.note: Its iodine 0.5 at n=3 from source 1055 is the same determination Frida carries on peanut butter 1162. Thom's decision is that one figure stands on both foods, since it is what the source measured for each. Peanut butter's chromium is borrowed from this row and is refused.

sesame-seeds.name: Sesame seeds, whole
sesame-seeds.note: "Sesamfrø, hele", the whole seed, against 471 "afskallede", the hulled one. Both carry the same EFSA code, so the Danish name is what separates them.

spinach-raw.name: Spinach, raw
spinach-raw.note: The unqualified row. 1741 is baby spinach, a different product.

kale-raw.name: Kale, raw
kale-raw.note: The unqualified row against Danish 1391, which reports chromium 0 at n=8 where this one reports 8.3 at n=44. They are also different kales: EFSA classifies 23 as stem kale and 1391 as curly. Taking the unqualified row is what lets Frida second-source chromium at all.

mushrooms-white-raw.name: Mushroom, raw
mushrooms-white-raw.note: "Champignon, rå", classified "Common mushrooms", which is Agaricus bisporus.

jerusalem-artichokes-raw.name: Jerusalem artichoke, raw
jerusalem-artichokes-raw.note: "Jordskok", against 57 "Artiskok", the globe artichoke, which the scorer ranks below it and grades proxy.

haricot-beans-cooked.name: White beans, dried and boiled
haricot-beans-cooked.note: Denmark's white bean, reached through ALIASES. "Hvide bønner, tørrede og kogt" is dried and boiled, the preparation this page's cooked legumes are.

dates.name: Date, dried
dates.note: "Daddel, tørret", and this page's dates are dried dates. Its chromium 80 at n=2 is the determination it shares with dried apricots 458; its iodine 1.8 at n=3 and its molybdenum are its own.

apple-raw-with-skin.name: Apple, raw, all varieties
apple-raw-with-skin.note: "Æble, uspec.", classified W/o core and W/o stem, so the skin is in it.

cherries-sweet-raw.name: Cherry, raw
cherries-sweet-raw.note: Frida's only raw cherry, and EFSA classifies it "Cherries (sweet)", which answers whether Denmark's cherry here is the sour one.

carrots-raw.name: Carrot, raw
carrots-raw.note: 24, 559 and 606 are all "Carrot, raw" in English. In Danish they are uspec., dansk and importeret, and an unqualified page food takes the unspecified row. Same rule as cauliflower 14, apple 2, brussels sprouts 41 and asparagus.

cucumber-raw-with-peel.name: Cucumber, raw
cucumber-raw-with-peel.note: Classified "Cucumbers" with no W/o peel facet, so the peel is in it.

grapes-raw.name: Grape, raw
grapes-raw.note: "Vindrue, rå", the unqualified row, against 508 "Vindrue, grønne", which is the green subset and borrows its iodine from this row.

tomatoes-raw.name: Tomato, ripe, raw, origin unknown
tomatoes-raw.note: "Tomat, uspec." against Danish 451 and imported 624, both of which borrow their biotin and iodine from this row.

olive-oil-extra-virgin.name: Olive oil
olive-oil-extra-virgin.note: Its chromium 6.8 at n=16 is one determination set Frida carries on olive, corn and refined soyabean oil alike. Refined soyabean oil is a page food and is not paired to Frida, so the figure reaches the page once.

romaine-lettuce-raw.name: Lettuce, Cos or romaine, raw
romaine-lettuce-raw.note: "Salat, Romaine, romersk". 1743 is "Salat, hjerte", lettuce hearts.

prunes-dried.name: Prune, dried plum
prunes-dried.note: "Sveske, rå", classified "Dried prunes, W/o stone". The Danish "rå" means unstewed rather than undried, one of the four rows in the release where a raw name and a processing classification agree rather than conflict. This is the row that used to lead raw plums, before the scorer stopped treating dried as raw.

dried-apricots-dried.name: Apricot, dried
dried-apricots-dried.note: Its chromium 80 at n=2, detected 59 to 100, is the same 1985 health-food-shop determination Frida carries on dried dates 533, which is also banked. Two page foods therefore rest on one determination set, as peanuts and peanut butter do. Banked on the same reading of Thom's rule: a figure a source reports for a food is that food's figure even where a neighbour shares it. Reversing this means unbanking dates or this, not both.

poppy-seeds.name: Poppy seeds
poppy-seeds.note: The row is called "Poppy seeds" and "Birkes, frø" and neither name mentions preparation, but EFSA classifies it as roasted and this page's poppy seeds are the plain seed. Eight of the ten rows Frida codes as roasted say so in their names and this is one of the two that do not. Its one cell is chromium 75.2 at n=7, detected 7.6 to 234.3.

peanut-butter-smooth.name: Peanut butter
peanut-butter-smooth.note: Its one admitted cell is the iodine determination it shares verbatim with peanuts 150. Banked on Thom's decision that the figure stands on both.

rye-bread.name: Rye bread, light
rye-bread.note: Frida has fourteen rye breads and no unspecified one. This page's rye bread is SR Legacy 18060, an American commercial rye, which is a mixed wheat and rye loaf; 413 is the only row EFSA classifies as "Mixed wheat and rye bread and rolls" without also naming a production place. It is also the only rye bread admitting molybdenum and boron, which is not the reason it was chosen.

pumpernickel.name: Rye bread, dark, pumpernickel
pumpernickel.note: Danish name and EFSA classification are both simply Pumpernickel.

swede-raw.name: Swede, raw
swede-raw.note: Its iodine 0.5 at n=3 is shared with instant mashed potato, which is not a page food.

sweetcorn-raw.name: Sweetcorn, on-the-cob, raw
sweetcorn-raw.note: "Majskolbe, rå", classified W/o cob, so the figure is for kernels. Its chromium 1 at n=3 is a figure Frida also carries on frozen strawberries and canned salmon, neither of which this page pairs to.
